title: Vascular contributions to cognitive decline and dementia
bottleneck: Mixed vascular and Alzheimer's pathology is the rule rather than the exception in late-life dementia, yet most drug development targets pure amyloid or tau. Small-vessel disease, blood-brain barrier breakdown, and impaired clearance interact with neurodegeneration in ways that are poorly quantified.
why_it_blocks: Ignoring the vascular half of dementia means trials enroll heterogeneous patients and therapies miss a major, potentially preventable driver of decline.
current_state: Intensive blood-pressure control has shown cognitive benefit, and vascular biomarkers are entering trials. No therapy specifically targets the vascular-neurodegenerative interface. Because vascular risk factors are modifiable, this is one of the few dementia avenues where prevention is already actionable through blood-pressure and lifestyle control. Yet dementia trials rarely stratify by vascular burden, muddying results.
